newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo wheat harvest ends on two thirds area - agency.
newsitem.headline: Yugo wheat harvest ends on two thirds area - agency.

text.p: Wheat has to date been harvested in Yugoslavia on two thirds of a total area of around 800,000 hectares, state news agency Tanjug quoted Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce official Milan Prostran as saying on Monday.
Nearly 2.3 million tonnes of wheat have been stockpiled in silos, Prostran said. In most districts, especially in fields belonging to agricultural enterprises, harvesting has been completed.
Only three to four days without rainfall are needed for the harvest to be completed, Prostran said.
Average yield in this year's wheat harvest, the longest in the past two decades due to frequent rains in July, is 3.8 tonnes per hectare.
Much of the new wheat has had to be dried due to moisture.
The Federal Statistics Office's latest wheat crop forecast based on the state of the crop on June 20 was 2.8 million tonnes with average yield of 3.44 tonnes per hectare.
